answers:
Where do my notes live?
+

Your notes are stored locally on your device. Lattice is a local-first notebook, so your device is the home for your research.

Can I take my notes somewhere else?
+

Yes. Export your notes as Markdown files, a readable format you can open in a text editor or use in other Markdown-compatible tools.

How do I back up my work?
+

Export your notes as files and keep a separate copy somewhere safe, such as an external drive. Backups are your responsibility; Lattice does not promise automatic cloud backup.

What happens if I cancel?
+

Cancellation has no effect on files you have already exported. Those Markdown files stay with you, and you can keep reading and using them independently of Lattice.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The desktop hero gives the large serif headline and the research-notebook illustration distinct columns. The dark primary button sits directly below the supporting explanation, while the navigation is quieter.
observations.implication: The eye can find the proposition, a concrete product representation and the next action without competing card clusters.

observations.observation: Serif display text, italic emphasis and small sans-serif explanatory text recur across sections. The display hierarchy is clear, but the notebook microcopy, workflow descriptions and FAQ answer use noticeably smaller text than the headings.
observations.implication: The page has an editorial character, while smaller explanatory details require closer reading, especially inside the scaled notebook illustration.

observations.observation: Ivory surfaces, dark green text, pale green panels, thin dividers and restrained arrow/star marks repeat consistently. The dark workflow band provides a clear change of section without introducing a new palette.
observations.implication: The hero, feature panel, pricing and FAQ appear to belong to one deliberate visual system.

observations.observation: The tilted notebook window includes a project list, a note, an attached source, tags and a separate question card. The Connect panel changes to linked question/note cards.
observations.implication: The illustrations make notes, source context and connections tangible. They remain illustrative interfaces rather than evidence of a working notebook product.

observations.observation: At the captured mobile width the headline, body copy, labelled Menu control and primary action fit the canvas. The notebook illustration begins within the first viewport, although most of its contents continue below it.
observations.implication: The opening communicates the main action promptly and hints at the product; reading the illustrated notebook requires scrolling. No obvious overlap or clipped primary text is visible in this capture.

observations.observation: The yearly prices are visually dominant and carry a nearby yearly label. The two plans have distinct but coordinated surfaces. The expanded FAQ uses a clear question/answer separation and leaves the other questions visible.
observations.implication: The captured pricing and answer states remain easy to scan. These observations describe presentation, not a numerical design score or a complete interaction audit.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score.

limits: Only the supplied captured states were reviewed. Mobile coverage here is the initial viewport, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
These static viewport captures do not evaluate motion quality, keyboard behavior, all scroll positions, every responsive breakpoint, or color contrast ratios.
Some anchored desktop captures start partway through a preceding heading; that is viewport framing, not evidence that the source page clips that heading.
The notebook mockups illustrate a fictional product. Their apparent controls are not evidence of implemented notebook functionality.
Both inspected candidates use a coherent serif-and-green editorial direction. These observations do not establish a general winner, causal improvement, or which condition produced either artifact.

processReview.summary: The baseline landing run planned browser verification, corrected a test’s keyboard modality and retested alongside responsive layout edits.

observations.observed: A public outline separated visual implementation from browser interaction and responsive verification.
The candidate built and ran a browser verifier, then a separate responsive/contrast helper and an HTML/syntax audit.

The first browser check failed on focus visibility after programmatic focus. The next command added actual Tab/Shift+Tab input, edited layout styles and reran the verifier successfully. The changed test preserved its visible-focus assertion.
The run retained browser scripts, captures and a README identifying Chrome-only verification and the illustrative product scope.

limits: The first verification script used an unsuitable input modality for its focus-visible assertion.
Test corrections and product changes occurred in one command, limiting attribution of each observed improvement.
Chrome-only candidate checks do not establish physical-device or cross-engine coverage.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
